China, HK stocks tumble as global tech selloff deepens
sum: HONG KONG: China and Hong Kong stocks fell on Friday as a Nasdaq-led tech rout rippled across Asia and fuelled fears the AI boom is losing steam, although bargain hunting helped pare losses in mainland markets buoyed by Beijing’s market-supporting measures.
China’s blue-chip CSI 300 Index dropped 1.4 percent, but notched up a 1.7 percent gain for the week to snap a 12-week-long losing streak.
The Shanghai Composite Index fell 1.1 percent on Friday, though it ended the week 1.4 percent higher, breaking a six-week run of declines.

In Hong Kong, the benchmark Hang Seng Index was down 1.3 percent but registered a 5.1 percent weekly gain, its best since March 2025. The Hang Seng Tech Index slid 1.8 percent on Friday, but posted its best weekly gain since February 2025, advancing 8.6 percent.

Tech sectors across Asia took a heavy blow after a steep selloff overnight in the US wiped trillions of dollars off market value, as investors fretted that a Democratic sweep in the US midterm elections could bring tighter scrutiny of the AI sector.
China’s tech-focused Star 50 Index and the AI Index slumped as much as 5.2 percent before paring some losses.
Dong Baozhen, chairman of asset manager Lingtong Shengtai, said the overnight slump in US tech stocks meant the logic behind the AI-driven rally had crumbled.

Hong Kong stocks open lower amid tech selloff
sum: Hong Kong shares opened lower on Friday, tracking a global tech sell-off as potential tighter artificial intelligence regulation rattled market sentiment.
The benchmark Hang Seng Index dropped 392 points, or 1.58 percent, to 24,404.
Lenovo (0992) kept slipping after logging a 6 percent loss a day ago, down 9.6 percent at the open, marking the worst performance among blue chips.

Chipmakers also dragged down the market. Hua Hong Grace Semiconductor (1347) fell 8.6 percent despite a 1.5 percent rise in third-quarter net profit released a day ago, while SMIC (0981) opened 6.4 percent lower.
Tech majors underperformed the market, with Alibaba (9988) and Tencent (0700) decreasing 3.8 percent and 2.2 percent.
In contrast, PetroChina (0857) and CNOOC (0883) went up 1.5 percent and 0.3 percent on the rebounding oil prices.

items.t: Hong Kong Stocks Surge on Heavy Volume: Hang Seng Index Rises 3.67%, Tencent, Alibaba and Other Tech Names Jump Over 7%
sum: On November 5, Hong Kong stocks pushed higher on heavy volume, with the Hang Seng Index closing up 3.67% and the Hang Seng Tech Index surging 5.55%, its biggest single-day gain since late February 2025.

Large-cap tech names strengthened across the board and served as the main engine driving the broader market. NetEase rose more than 9%, Alibaba and Xiaomi gained over 8%, Tencent Holdings climbed more than 7%, and JD.com and Meituan rose nearly 7%. Gold shares also advanced broadly, with Laopu Gold up more than 8% and Zhaojin Mining up over 5%. Consumer, auto, property and biopharma sectors posted the largest gains, while oil and petrochemicals, coal and semiconductors declined.
Fund flows were mixed. Southbound Funds recorded net selling of more than HK$21.3 billion (approximately $2.7 billion) on the day, in contrast to the sharp index rally.

Optical communications, memory and PCB concept stocks lagged, with Yangtze Optical Fibre and Cable down more than 12% and Kingboard Laminates down more than 12%. Zhongji Innolight, CIG and Montage Technology each fell more than 6%, while GigaDevice dropped over 5%.

Hong Kong stocks drop at open
sum: Hong Kong shares fell at the open on Wednesday as investors awaited the outcome of the US midterm elections.
The benchmark Hang Seng Index decreased 74 points, or 0.32 percent, to 23,451.
Biopharmaceutical stocks outperformed the market. Wuxi Biologics (2269) and BeOne Medicines (6160) jumped 2.2 percent and 2.1 percent, marking the two largest gains at the opening bell.
Hansoh Pharmaceutical (3692) and Wuxi Apptec (2359) followed with growths of 1.8 percent and 17 percent, respectively.
Tech giants opened mixed. JD.com (9618) and Xiaomi (1810) slipped 1.8 percent and 1.7 percent, while Baidu (9888) inched up 0.8 percent.
Alibaba (9988) retreated 0.8 percent, and Tencent (0700) rose 0.15 percent.
Lenovo (9992) recovered from the 6 percent decline a day ago, up 1.7 percent at the open.

Hong Kong Stock Exchange Today: Hang Seng Index Rises to 23,393.32 Amid Ukraine-Russia Talks and Iran-US Negotiations
sum: Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index rose 0.42% to 23,393.32 on Monday 2 November 2026, its second straight gain, as the Hang Seng Tech Index surged 2.25% led by Xiaomi, CATL, Alibaba and Tencent, while banks and gold miners lagged.

The Hang Seng Index, the main benchmark of the Hong Kong Stock Exchange, closed at 23,393.32 on Monday, up 98.90 points or 0.42%, according to Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing data reported by Xinhua and The Standard. It followed Friday's 1.5% rebound and marked the index's first session of November in positive territory.

The index traded as high as 23,543.30 but gave back part of those gains in the afternoon. The more significant move came in technology: the Hang Seng Tech Index jumped 2.25% to 3,839.41 after rising as much as 3% intraday, while the Hang Seng China Enterprises Index added 0.56% to 7,906.11. Full-day turnover reached HK$204.84 billion.

Two forces supported the market. First, expectations of fresh policy support in mainland China lifted sentiment, after regulators met banks and brokers to discuss stabilising the equity market and the People's Bank of China signalled a new liquidity operation. Chinese brokerage stocks were among the leaders as investors bet on higher trading volumes.

Second, easing oil prices and a recovery in US stock futures after Friday's technology sell-off gave investors confidence to buy back into beaten-down tech names ahead of Apple's quarterly results. Even so, the gain in the broader Hang Seng was modest because banks and gold-related stocks, which had served as havens in October, were sold to fund purchases elsewhere.

Xiaomi was the best-performing blue chip, rising 6.1%, followed closely by battery giant CATL, which gained about 6% as lithium battery shares rallied. Among the heavyweights, Alibaba climbed 2.5% and Tencent advanced 2.2%, together providing a large share of the index's points gain.

Chipmakers also recovered. Hua Hong Semiconductor rose nearly 3% and SMIC added 1.5%. Casino operators climbed despite a decline in Macao's October gaming revenue, with Galaxy Entertainment up 3.7% and Sands China up 3.1%. On the downside, Bank of China and BOC Hong Kong were among the weakest constituents after their recent results, and gold miners eased.

Southbound capital withdrew for a record 13 consecutive days, yet the Hang Seng Index rose instead—this market keeps rewarding a mistake.
sum: Weekly Review: Examining the "rewarded mistake" through the lens of southbound funds in Hong Kong stocks.

Close on Oct 30,$Hang Seng Index (800000.HK)$ at 23,294.42 points, up 0.87% for the week, ending two consecutive weeks of declines; $Hang Seng TECH Index (800700.HK)$ at 3,754.90 points, down 3.02% for the week; the SOE Index rose 1.37% for the week.

But what is truly glaring is not the indices, but the capital flows: Southbound funds recorded net sales of HKD 3.56 billion on Oct 30. This marks the 13th consecutive trading day of net selling, setting a new record for the longest streak of continuous net outflows, with cumulative outflows totaling HKD 37.323 billion over the 13-day period.Net outflows for the entire month of October approached HKD 28 billion, the largest single-month figure since July 2021.
Money is flowing out on one side, while indices are rising on the other.

The structural divergence is also stark: On Oct 30, consumer and energy sectors led the gains— $MAO GEPING (01318.HK)$ up over 13%, $MENGNIU DAIRY (02319.HK)$ up over 9%, $SINOPEC CORP (00386.HK)$ up 6.22%, $PETROCHINA (00857.HK)$ up 5.66%; meanwhile, the semiconductor sector continues to face pressure,$SMIC (00981.HK)$ down over 4%, $GIGADEVICE (03986.HK)$ down more than 8%. Looking at the full week,$SMIC (00981.HK)$ Down 8.67%, with southbound capital withdrawing approximately RMB 4.1 billion from it over the past seven days.
[But what is most worth pondering is this month's "rebound"]
The Hang Seng TECH Index fell 11.73% in October, declining steadily. Throughout this process, almost every minor rebound was beaten back by selling pressure.
